# Infrastructure at Scale {#infrastructure-at-scale}

#### 2004 - 2016 · UC Santa Cruz, UC Berkeley, UCLA

::: {.chapter-intro}
The projects in this chapter run at a scale most people cannot visualize: exabytes of storage, an open instruction set for chips, and the compute infrastructure for modern AI. They started as dissertations, summer projects, and PhD students frustrated with rewriting the same Python code. They ended up as global standards, hardware architectures, and the nervous system of the internet.
:::

---

## Ceph: The Dissertation That Funded an OSPO {#ceph}

**The project:** Ceph distributed storage system
**Campus:** UC Santa Cruz (Storage Systems Research Center)
**Period:** 2004
**Key figures:** Sage Weil (PhD student), Scott A. Brandt (advisor)

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### The direct line to this document

The money from Ceph's commercialization [@weil2006ceph] funded CROSS at UCSC. CROSS became the first UC OSPO. The UC OSPO Network grew from CROSS. This history was written by an organization that exists because one dissertation was released with an open license and commercialized responsibly.

{{< on-campus ceph >}}

## RISC-V: An Open Instruction Set from Berkeley {#riscv}

**The project:** RISC-V open instruction set architecture
**Campus:** UC Berkeley
**Period:** May 2010 (Parallel Computing Laboratory) [@riscv2026about]
**Key figures:** Krste Asanovic, David Patterson, Andrew Waterman, Yunsup Lee

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### What it became

RISC-V [@riscv2019] is an open, royalty-free instruction set architecture. RISC-V International listed 305 member organizations in November 2026 [@riscv2026members] and reported members in 70 countries in December 2024 [@riscv2024redmond]. In March 2020, the RISC-V International Association was incorporated in Switzerland [@riscv2026about].

{{< on-campus riscv >}}

## Named Data Networking: Rethinking the Internet {#ndn}

**The project:** Named Data Networking (NDN / NFD)
**Campus:** UCLA
**Period:** 2010 (as a Future Internet Architecture project)
**Key figures:** Lixia Zhang (Lead PI, Professor of Computer Science)

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### Why this belongs here

NDN is not finished infrastructure - it is active research into what the internet could become. It belongs in this document because NSF funded it as a Future Internet Architecture project led from UCLA, starting with $7.9 million in 2010 [@ucla2010ndn], and because it represents the UC system's ongoing contribution to internet architecture, not just applications running on top of it.

{{< on-campus ndn >}}

## Ray: From RISELab to the PyTorch Foundation {#ray}

**The project:** Ray distributed computing framework
**Campus:** UC Berkeley RISELab
**Period:** 2016
**Key figures:** Robert Nishihara, Philipp Moritz, Ion Stoica, Michael Jordan

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### What it became

Ray [@moritz2018ray] is a framework for scaling Python and AI workloads from a laptop to a cluster. In October 2025, Anyscale, the company founded by Ray's creators, contributed Ray to the PyTorch Foundation, which is part of the Linux Foundation [@lf2025ray].

{{< on-campus ray >}}
